Stat time!

Since 1995, the $SPX in November has had only 6 red months.

That's a 81% win rate for November.

Three of those red months were:

-.83%
-.51%
-.23%

Nothing. Flat af. lol

However, the other 3 red months were:

-7.48% (Nov 2008)
-4.40% (Nov 2007)
-8.01% (Nov 2000)

Scary, but look at the year right?

In addition, the $SPX is up 13 of the last 14 Novembers, 2021 being the outlier. Ironically, 2021 was one of the best performing SPX years in history too.

i'm starting to think we could be near the end of this macro cycle for equities

a lot of the stocks that have led the market since late 2022 are sitting on massive gains, and we're finally seeing some meaningful profit-taking after years without a major correction

crypto started showing weakness earlier, which could explain why it bottomed ahead of equities and bounced so strongly in Q3

the question i'm trying to figure out now is whether that bounce marked the beginning of a new bull market or was simply a countertrend rally within a larger downtrend

if it's the latter, i think a lot of people are going to get caught off guard

It's been one week since @vladtenev talked about Robinhood Chain during Q3 earnings.

Since then, neither he nor @JohannKerbrat have made a post or reply regarding it (or anything) on X.

While this could very likely mean they're working hard behind the scenes, it's important they're both aware how integral making the social side of an L1 a priority is to its long term success.

That in no way means shilling new coins or projects every day.

It means actively spending time talking about what you've built, what you're building, and most importantly interacting with people who use your products.

A simple reply here and there goes a long way.

I have noticed the @RobinhoodCrypto account start to step up its game and interact a bit more with various communities, which is encouraging.

But at the end of the day, people care about leadership more than anything else.

While X might not be one of their core products, the community that exists on X - the builders, the traders, and the projects - are the rails of what makes the ecosystem successful.

So Vlad, if you'd truly like to optimize your use of time moving forward to make Robinhood Chain "even bigger" and answer the question for "how to support the community," just have your team show up and engage more often.

That's the ramp up you (and we) really need.

And if no one on the team is willing to spend that time to make it happen, find someone who you can put in a position of leadership that does.

Best regards,

Kaleo
